source.author: verg
source.text: Ei mihi, qualis erat, quantum mutatus ab illo Hectore, qui redit exuvias indutus Achilli, vel Danaum Phrygios iaculatus puppibus ignis, squalentem barbam et concretos sanguine crinis volneraque illa gerens, quae circum plurima muros accepit patrios.
source.text_original: Ei mihi, qualis erat, quantum mutatus ab illo / Hectore, qui redit exuvias indutus Achilli, / vel Danaum Phrygios iaculatus puppibus ignis, / squalentem barbam et concretos sanguine crinis / volneraque illa gerens, quae circum plurima muros / accepit patrios.
source.text_english: Ah me, what a sight he was, how changed from that Hector who returns, clothed in Achilles’ spoils, or having hurled Phrygian fire against the Danaans’ ships, bearing a bristling beard and hair clotted with blood and those wounds that he had received in great number around his native walls.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: rara et sponte patet, siquando pectore ductor vulnera nota gerens, galeis praefixa rotisque cui domus aut studium mortales pellere curas, culta fides, longe metus atque ignota cupido, seu venit in vittis castaque in veste sacerdos.
reuse.text_original: rara et sponte patet, siquando pectore ductor / vulnera nota gerens, galeis praefixa rotisque / cui domus aut studium mortales pellere curas, / culta fides, longe metus atque ignota cupido, / seu venit in vittis castaque in veste sacerdos.
reuse.text_english: It is seldom open, and only of its own accord, if ever the leader, bearing in his breast the known wounds, comes forth. It is the man whose house or passion is to drive mortal cares away, whose fidelity is cultivated, and far from whom are fear and unknown desire, or the priest comes in ribbons and in chaste vesture.
